title: Policy Provisions on Rescission for a Materially Untrue Health Answer
content:
A policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies issued on an answer to a health question that was materially untrue may be rescinded, which means treating it as never having come into force.

### The window in which it may be done

The plan rescinds no later than the last day of the contestability period counted from the policy effective date. The effective date, the policy and the right it was issued on are read from the policy record, correlated by that policy, before the rescission is made. Calendar months are counted from the day of the month the policy took effect, a month with no matching day ends on its last day, the final day of the period is itself inside it, and calendar days are never used in place of calendar months. The length of the period is the number of calendar months the plan letter carries as its contestability period.

Where that period runs 24 calendar months, a rescission made on the day of the month the policy took effect in the twenty-fourth month is made on the final day of the period and is in time; a rescission made the day after is not.

After the contestability period the policy may not be rescinded for anything the applicant said at issue, however the plan later views it, and a policyholder asking whether their old answers can still be used against them is told plainly that they cannot.

### What makes a misstatement material

A misstatement is material only where the plan would not have issued the policy, or would have issued it on different terms, had it known; an answer that would have changed nothing is never a ground.

### Policies that are never rescinded on a health answer

A policy issued during open enrollment or on a guaranteed issue right is never rescinded for a health answer, because no health answer was allowed to matter.

### What rescission does

On rescission every premium paid is returned and every benefit paid is recovered, and the policyholder is told in writing what was found and how to dispute it.

### An innocent error

An innocent error of fact, such as a wrong date of birth, is not a rescission ground: the premium is put right from issue and the difference billed or refunded.
